quote: FT_HT-MEDOC-DE-DAUZAC-2016.pdf

Mooie donkerrode kleur met bijna zwarte reflexen in het glas. De wijn is helder en zuiver. Zeer donker. De neus is nog zeer gesloten, maar alle tekenen van een enorm aromatisch potentieel zijn aanwezig: de diepte, de complexiteit en het al perfect geïntegreerde hout van de rijping op barrique. Enkele klassieke tonen van viooltje, maar alles nog zeer ingehouden. In de mond is de aanzet zeer zacht en zijdeachtig. Daarna vult de wijn, met behoud van diezelfde zachtheid, geleidelijk de mond met een enorme lengte, zozeer dat je je afvraagt hoe lang het nog kan doorgaan. De middenmond is perfect in balans. Hij is zeer dicht, met strakke tannine die nog zeer delicaat is. De wijn heeft een opmerkelijke persistentie en volheid in de mond en laat niet de geringste onbalans of zwakte zien.

how.agreed: the document and the filename name the same estate
how.another property: the sheet names a property this dashboard does not hold, such as Soutard-Cadet
how.disagree: the document and the filename name different estates
how.from a negociant’s property pages: a technical sheet linked from a Bordeaux negociant’s page for the property, where the estate itself publishes none
how.from the document: the estate is named in the sheet itself
how.from the estate’s own page of technical: a sheet linked from the estate’s technical-sheets page, which is built in the browser and empty until rendered
how.from the estate’s own sitemap: a technical sheet linked from a page the site’s own sitemap lists, which the media API did not answer for
how.from the estate’s own vintage pages: a sheet linked from a vin.co vintage page under a per-vintage code, named by the server rather than by the site
how.from the estate’s own vintage posts: a post on the estate’s own site, one per wine per vintage, read through the WordPress REST API because the page that shows it is built in the browser
how.from the filename: only the filename names the estate
how.from the folder, which serves one estate: nothing in the file names an estate, and every other sheet on that site resolves to one
how.from the name of the page: a crawled page whose own filename names the estate, where the folder it was saved in does not
how.from the name of the sheet: a sheet whose own filename names the estate, where the folder it was saved in does not
how.from the name this session gave it: downloaded here from a directory that names one slug per wine, so the filename identifies the wine and the text, which carries the owning house on every sheet, does not
how.from the site’s own media library: a file WordPress lists under /wp-json/wp/v2/media, which answers for every upload and does not need the page that shows it to be rendered
how.read out of the document, the filename s: a sheet whose filename is a hash or an upload timestamp, opened so that the vintage and the estate could be read from the page itself
how.the property’s press dossier, not a vint: a press dossier a house publishes per property rather than per vintage; it is registered so that it is not fetched and read again
how.unidentified: nothing in the file names an estate

documentation.note: Which wine and vintage each source sheet belongs to. The app does not load this; it is provenance, so that a record citing a sheet can be checked against the wine that sheet is for. The sheets themselves are not in this repository.

roles.combined: one sheet covering both the red and the white, so either may cite it
roles.grand: the grand vin, the wine the estate is judged on
roles.other: another cuvee, often the dry white
roles.page: a page crawled from the estate's own site
roles.skip: not a technical sheet - a brochure or a press review
roles.unknown: on disk but not identified - the document names no estate this dashboard holds
